en: The Ritual Manual for the Five Great Ox-Jewel Rain-Treasure Dhāraṇī,
translated by Vajragarbha. At that time,
the Tathāgata was in the secret palace of the Vajraśekhara Yoga, together with [bodhisattvas] as numerous as the atoms of the universe.
The great assembly gathered together, and he proclaimed the subtle, profound, and secret teachings.
At that time, within the assembly, there was a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Ākāśa-ṛddhi-rāja (King of Space-like Supernatural Powers).
He rose from his seat, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, throughout immeasurable kalpas in the past, I have made offerings..."
It nourishes all Buddhas and practices the most supreme secret teachings. It is the *pañcamahāgavendraratnavarṣa-dhāraṇī*.
This is the most profound, secret, subtle, and auspicious great jewel-treasury of all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones;
it serves as a resource for sentient beings of the degenerate age—whether householders or renunciants—who are impoverished, suffering, and of meager merit.
"Those who possess few things and whose requests and aspirations do not accord with their wishes—may I cause all their aspirations to be fulfilled. I wish to preach this Dharma;
I only pray that the World-Honored One will, out of compassion, grant me permission. At that time, the Tathāgata praised him, saying, "Excellent!
Speak according to your intention. In the past, during incalculable kalpas, while I was on the stage of a bodhisattva, I made a great power of vows for the sake of..."
May all those sentient beings who fill the ocean of the entire dharma-realm— those of meager merit and inferior capacity in this Sahā world—
be transformed into great water oxen with jade and silver hooves, golden horns, and the color of blue lapis lazuli,
possessing great power and pervading the dharma-realm for the sake of all sentient beings. May you manifest according to their various types to bring about great benefit, just as you do now.
Daily, he made this great vow: "If you wish to preach this Jewel-Rain Dhāraṇī, it is the supreme secret cow-jewel seal of all Buddhas, a profound esoteric art that benefits all living beings."
At that time, the Great Being, the Bodhisattva Ākāśavidyādhara-śrī-vajragarbha, having received the Buddha’s permission,
spoke these verses before the Tathāgata:
"Relying upon the supreme vehicle of all Buddhas, I shall proclaim the Secret Yoga named 'Rain of Jewels'."
This is for those of meager merit in the age of the Dharma’s semblance; the Buddha taught this profound method of accomplishment.
If there are sentient beings lacking merit and wisdom, none of their desires will accord with their hearts.
Due to this poverty and suffering, they commit evil karma and fall into the three miserable realms from which there is no time of escape.

By practicing the secret dharma as I have taught, one shall study the *Vajra-dhāraṇī for Raining Jewels* and be liberated from the hardships of poverty and suffering; all the wishes of the heart shall be fulfilled.
If, within my great compassionate vow of universal salvation, there were even a single person who did not achieve these two-fold aspirations, may I never attain enlightenment.
"I have fallen into the suffering of the sin of falsehood; I shall not return to original enlightenment and abandon great compassion.

Having spoken this verse, he then recited the dharani-method: with the two hands bound externally, the two *vāyu* fingers are joined upright and pressed together like the shape of a jewel. The mantra:
Oṃ vajratara svāhā.
Furthermore, it is said that for the root dhāraṇī, one should join the palms in the vajra-mudrā: Oṃ bandha liśvara jaṭhara svāhā.
Next, the root heart-seal mantras of the five great ox-jewels are explained. First is the Dharma-realm Ox-jewel Seal:
form the vajra outer-bind with the middle fingers like needles. The mantra:
Oṃ vajra-ratna svāhā. Next is the mantra for the Vajra-Ox-Jewel Seal (*vajra-go-ratna-mudrā*).

Form the outer vajra-bind with the *kṣānti* (ring finger) and *samaya* (pinky) fingers standing upright, and the *vīrya* (middle finger) and *bala* (index finger) fingers bent inward, shaped like a three-pronged vajra. The mantra is: Oṃ vajra-ratna svāhā.
Oṃ vajra hūṃ svāhā. Next is the Jewel-Light-Ox-Jewel Seal (Ratnārci-go-maṇi-mudrā).
Form the outer vajra-bind; extend the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers while the *vīrya* and *bala* fingers are joined in the shape of a jewel. The mantra:
Oṃ vajra-tara svāhā. Next is the mantra of the Lotus-Ox-Jewel Seal.
The mantra for the vajra-bāhyabandha (outer binding) with the thumbs and index fingers formed like a lotus is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-hrīḥ svāhā. Next is the mantra of the Karma-cow-jewel mudrā: Form the vajra-outer-bind;

extend the *kṣānti* (patience) and *praṇidhāna* (vow) fingers and join their tips; extend the *śīla* (precept), *dhyāna* (meditation), and *vīrya* (effort) fingers and interlace them with one another. True.
He said:
"Oṃ vajra aḥ svāhā.
Next, the method of practice is explained.
If one wishes to practice this supreme dharma, with the three karmas purified and having personally received the ritual manual from a virtuous teacher, one should first undergo empowerment.
Then, in a mountain retreat, a quiet place, a temple, or wherever one prefers, one should establish a mandala.
Constructing a square mandala according to its required dimensions, one should place the sacred image upon the surface of the mandala.
Regarding its iconographic form:
its body is golden in color, with four arms and one face. On its crown it wears five *gośīrṣa* gems, which constitute the five-Buddha jeweled tiara.
Its left hand cradles the solar disc, and its right hand cradles the lunar disc. The left hand holds a wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*) at the heart, while the right hand...

Form the mudrā of granting fearlessness, with the hands slightly apart, positioned as if upon a jewel. The practitioner should face the image at the eastern side of the maṇḍala and perform recitation.
Scatter various seasonal flowers upon the maṇḍala, and offer incense, lamps, food, and fruit according to one’s means, as an act of worship.
Whenever entering the maṇḍala, prostrate oneself before the honored image, bowing with all five limbs to pay homage to all [the buddhas].
Having performed the confession, rejoicing, entreaty, and making of vows before the Buddha and the assembly of noble ones,

one should then sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) or the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*), or sit as is convenient. With body upright and mindfulness established, one should constantly apply fragrant ointment to both hands,
join the palms with the hollows facing upward, and recite the mantra for purifying the three karmas.
Oṃ śūnyatājñānavajrasvabhāvātmako ’haṃ svāhā.
Next is the heart-seal mantra of the Buddha Family,
the Vajra-Palm-Union (Vajra-añjali) mantra.
Oṃ īna īga svāhā.
Next is the heart-seal mantra of the Lotus Family (in the golden casket):
Oṃ arulika svāhā.
Next is the Heart Mudrā of the Vajra Family (in a golden casket): Oṃ vajradhṛk svāhā.
Next is the Armor for Protecting the Body mudrā and mantra.
Form the *vajramuṣṭi* (diamond-fist) mudrā with both hands. Place the left fist at the left hip. With the right fist, seal five locations:
the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ bhūrjvāra hūṃ. Next, perform the mudrā and mantra for summoning the deity: Form the inner-binding with both hands;
extend the right wind-finger (anāmikā) and slightly bend it into the shape of a hook, and summon three times. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ jra hūṃ trā kṛ e he hi svāhā. Next is the mantra of the body-seal of Cundā.

Form the double-hand bind (*añjali-bandha*). Hold the tips of the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers together. Extend the *madhyamā* and *aṅguṣṭha* fingers, bending them so that they touch the backs of the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* without joining them, forming the shape of a three-pronged vajra. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ amṛte hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Next, offer the arghya water seal.
On the left and right sides of the maṇḍala, place a pure vessel in each, filled with scented water, to serve as the arghya. First, perform the invitation.
At that time, those [offerings] for the right side are presented; later, when escorting [the deity], those for the left side are presented.
When making the offering, one holds the *argha* vessel with both hands at the forehead and recites the mantra while bathing the feet of the principal deity (*bimba*). The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajranāgata hūṃ. Next, perform the flower-seat mudrā:
join the two hands with palms hollowed together to form the eight-petaled blooming lotus mudrā at the forehead. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kamala svāhā.
Next is the seal for general offerings:

join both palms together; bind the two fingers of the *śīla* (ring) direction outward; and with the *vīrya* (middle) and *bala* (third) fingers, curve them inward like a jewel shape. Thus it is bound.
The mudrā is now formed. Recite the mantra:
Oṃ gaganasambhava vajra hoḥ. Visualize that from the mudrā there arise immeasurable varieties of offering substances:
incense, flowers, lamps, light, unguents, food, drink, and jewels.
With banners, pennants, canopies, and all manner of precious objects, offer worship to the Honored One and the entire assembly of noble ones.
Next, form the Vajra-joined-palms mudrā and recite the praise to the Bodhisattva Mahāgovinda as follows:
Vajra-ratna-svavajra-ratha-vajra-kṣama-mahāmani-ākṣepa-garbha-vajra-tva-vajra-garbha namaḥ sradhite.
Next, for the *karmamudrā*: form the left fist at the heart; join the thumbs and ring fingers (the space and wind elements) in the shape of a jewel.
With the right hand, make the gesture of granting boons (*varadamudrā*). Visualize that one's own body is identical to the Bodhisattva Mahāgovinda. The mantra:

Oṃ jvaḥ hūṃ traḥ hrīḥ aḥ haṃ svāhā. Next, bind the samaya-mudrā: with the two hands joined externally in the *baddha* gesture, bend the forefingers and middle fingers back toward each other in the shape of a jewel.
Extend the ring fingers and little fingers together and place them at the heart. This is the True [Mudrā].
He said:
"Oṃ vajraratna hūṃ. Then, taking a crystal rosary and placing it in the palm of his hand at his heart, he recited the consecration mantra for the rosary three times.
Pervasive. The mantra is:
Oṃ vilokita-māra svāhā. Then, one should make this aspiration:
"Beginning with my own person, for all sentient beings, regarding all that they desire and all worldly [matters]..."
"May it be well. By the power of my recitation, may [this] be swiftly accomplished. With a humble mind, one should perform the recitation above the heart while chanting this mantra.
Within seven days, having completed three hundred thousand recitations, the Noble One will appear before the practitioner;
whatever is sought according to one's heart's desire shall all be accomplished.
If one constantly maintains this recitation, performing it three times each day with one thousand and eighty repetitions per session,
once the count reaches one million repetitions, no requested aspiration will fail to be fulfilled. Upon completing the prescribed number of recitations, place the rosary upon the crown of your head,
offer prayers for what you seek, and then return it to its original place.
Next, perform the ritual for escorting the Honzon (the Principal Deity) by means of the mudrā and mantra.
Form the outer-bind with both hands, extend the two thumbs upward, and insert their tips into the flower. Recite the mantra while visualizing the Honzon being escorted back to his original realm.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajratāre. Next, don the armor as before.
Relying upon the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment, I shall proclaim this profound and subtle Dharma. Should there be those who lack faith during the final age of the image...

People differ; one must not bestow [this] upon anyone indiscriminately. First, select a disciple whose mental conduct is revered by others, who possesses wisdom, cultivates the four immeasurables, delights in the Mahāyāna, and maintains a mind of reverence for the Triple Gem and universal compassion.
Once they have entered the maṇḍala under a teacher and received empowerment (*abhiṣeka*), and having been granted authorization (*anujñā*), they may practice.
Do not allow them to act as they please or to rely on this profound Dharma without guidance. Vajrasattva.
Administer secret governance and punishment. Filially support your parents without indolence. Reverently honor and respect your ācārya.

With a sincere heart, believe in and accept this Great Dharma, never giving rise to even a single thought of lack of faith. After receiving the transmission, cultivate this exclusively. With a sincere heart, pray for whatever you seek;
may the Honored One take pity and bestow protection, so that siddhi appears before you and all wishes are fulfilled. If...
One should have no weary heart when others come to seek [the teachings], bestowing them according to one's capacity.

One should offer precious jewels to the *ācārya* who transmits the lineage, not sparing even body or life. If one is stingy and does not practice according to this dharma, *siddhi* will not be perfected.
If one suddenly forbids its proclamation in the world, one will fall into the evil realms due to the sin of slander. Therefore, this mudrā is kept secret.

Because it is esoteric, the karmic obstacles of the six sense faculties are entirely purified; merit and wisdom are perfected, and one possesses great conduct, destined to realize unsurpassed, great Bodhi.
The Ritual Manual for the *Gomayamaṇiratnavarṣa-dhāraṇī*.
The Venerable Jichie of Kokuzan showed this to him. Because this Dharma is extremely secret, it was never circulated.

However, when Great Master Chikaku was about to pass away, fearing that this Dharma might be lost, he transmitted it to him, though he kept it deeply hidden within his heart and soul, not daring to reveal it.
He said, "Only when you can recognize a worthy vessel may you transmit and receive it. Thus it is said.
Extracted from the *Cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī-vidhi*.

On the third day of the first month in the third year of Bunpō, this was completed at the residence of the head priest of the Tōnan-in (Southeast Court) within the Hon-in of Fudōji, based on the manuscript from the Shinnō-bō.
Do not let it pass beyond the bamboo and wooden screens.
Vajra-saṃbhāra-citta (37-22)
